title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 19, 2026
headline: LaFleur praised Bam Knight's relief start and Josh Sweat's edge play, said Garrett Williams is doing well at safety, and gave an ankle update on Walt Wed/Thu before Denver.
summary: LaFleur said the defense's performance was the standard the team wants to reproduce, comparing its unified, aggressive play to the 2024 unit. He said the red zone was the main problem: the offense was efficient between the 20s but settled for field goals inside the 20, and the team fell from a strong ranking to around fifth. He called the fixes clear but not easy and said the staff has new ideas for the downhill run game. He praised Bam Knight for stepping in and running hard, and said Josh Sweat was a force on the edge with production. He said Garrett Williams is handling his move to safety well given the injuries there. On the injury front, he gave only a limited update on the ankle issue for Walt, promising more information Wednesday or Thursday. He said the 13-personnel usage is helping the offense, and that the pin-and-pull runs are a change of pace the team is building on. He took responsibility for a late play-call penalty that led to an illegal formation, and said he trusts special teams coordinator Monty on kicking matters.

injuries.detail: Asked about an ankle injury coming out of the game; LaFleur said more information would come Wednesday or Thursday.

signals.claim: Stepped in and ran hard in the win, with the coach praising his toughness and performance; a larger role is plausible but not stated.
signals.note: A positive review of an unexpected starter increases the chance he keeps a meaningful workload if the starter is still out.

signals.note: A strong performance and coach praise support his pass-rush role and sack upside against Denver.

signals.note: A cornerback who is now playing safety may see more snaps and a broader role, which matters for IDP and DB depth.

topics.detail: LaFleur said the defense played with a unified, aggressive style that was reminiscent of 2024 and set a standard for the team, and that the offense's struggles were partly caused by the defense.
The offense was efficient outside the 20 but struggled inside it and settled for field goals. LaFleur said the team will need better scheming and that the ranking will drop from around 13th.
LaFleur took the blame for a late play-call penalty on a screen. He said special teams coordinator Monty handles kicking and punting, and he praised the kicker's performance.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Monday, October 19th | Press Conference
headline: AJ Terrell's return from IR is trending toward this week, and Jahan Dotson's role in the offense is getting praise.
summary: Stefanski opened by saying Kendal Daniels is doing well, is back in the building, and was released from the hospital and back in the locker room after the game, though he has no update on his status for the next game. He said the team is still awaiting imaging on several players. He called the Week 6 loss to the Bears a self-inflicted loss, crediting Chicago but saying Atlanta had hurt itself and needed to own its mistakes across all phases. He said the offense was forced into tempo for much of the fourth quarter, which took the run game out of the plan. On the pass rush, he said Michael Penix Jr. had to handle heavy blitzing and that the offense did not make defenses pay enough, though he praised Penix's processing and progression work. He said Atlanta's secondary and pass rush must work together and that corners are expected to handle tough matchups. He said the Cooper Rush move was made because Andy was available and the team is always looking to add to the roster. He described Jack Strand as getting extra developmental reps and said the Andy addition doesn't affect Strand's situation. The next opponent is the 49ers at home.

title: Jesse Minter on Browns Loss, Lamar Jackson's Status
headline: Lamar Jackson is day-to-day with a Wednesday update pending; Trey Hendrickson and Ja'Kobi Lane look good after returns, while Keyon Martin reclaimed a dime role from Chandler Rivers.
summary: Minter opened by calling the Week 6 loss to Cleveland disappointing and said the team failed to capitalize on chances to pull away after halftime, especially on special teams and defense. He said the offense struggled against Cleveland's aggressive run defense, which attacked Derrick Henry and the wide zone scheme, and that the Browns' coverage manned up and used some effective change-ups. On Lamar Jackson, Minter said he is still day-to-day and the team will know more on Wednesday, and that he may practice this week. Minter praised Ja'Kobi Lane's first game back, citing his catches, physicality and blocking, while expecting bigger jumps as he gets into rhythm. He said a player he referred to as Kim Jordan (name garbled in captions) has come a long way in concussion protocol and could return this week, with a final decision expected soon. On defense, Minter credited Keyon Martin and said the team moved Martin back into the dime package after Chandler Rivers had filled in; Rivers has practiced well, and the switch back was a judgment call. Trey Hendrickson's first game back went well, and Minter felt good about how he exited the game, while Rashod Bateman was dealing with an end-of-game issue but there is optimism he will be fine. Minter also discussed balancing Hendrickson and Mike Green on the right side and said the team is working on finding the right alignments to use both. Minter acknowledged operational issues with the offense, such as delay-of-game penalties, and said the kicking situation is a results-driven concern, but declined to say if another kicker would be added. He closed by framing the next game as a division matchup and stressing week-to-week preparation.

title: Joe Brady Discusses Gardner-Johnson Suspension, Injury Updates, Self Scouting, And More
headline: Gardner-Johnson faces a league suspension and his return role is uncertain; DJ Moore's status stays unclear, while Keon Coleman and James Cook were praised for their recent play.
summary: Brady said S C.J. Gardner-Johnson's league suspension stemmed from an inexcusable on-field incident that cost the team a player for the rest of the game, and the team addressed it privately and in front of the group. He framed the team's penalty problem as the bigger concern and said Gardner-Johnson has to play better, though he did not directly commit to a starting job on his return. Brady said the bye week is a chance to self-scout with fresh eyes, since the team has six games of tape and is 5-1 but not satisfied. He credited the pass rush for consistent hits on the quarterback even without a sack, and said the coverage and contested-ball work were good. On the passing game, he said Keon Coleman has made plays when given opportunities, and that Josh Allen stayed calm through the changes without DJ Moore. Brady praised special teams, especially the kickoff coverage and Greg Dortch's effort, and said the unit was penalty-free. He said James Cook had a strong game with ball security, but the team needs to manage his workload over a 20-game season. The Ravens in Week 8 are the next priority, with self-scouting coming first.

title: Dave Canales: 'A man with options is blessed'
headline: Tommy Tremble had his best game, Tershawn Wharton played a full game back, and Monroe Freeling's return and starting spot remain undecided.
summary: Canales praised the win as a three-phase effort and credited the Eagles' front while calling the defense's back-to-back games holding opponents to 50 or fewer rushing yards a great stretch. He said the offense stayed with its approach and finished on its terms, and he was critical of penalties that were largely byproducts of aggressive play. Tershawn Wharton played a full game of about 80 snaps after returning, and Canales said the strength and training staffs had him fit enough to finish. Taylor Moton showed splash plays in his return, and Trevor Etienne was consistent on punt returns. Canales said Monroe Freeling's situation is still being worked through, with his physical status and how he responds to training to determine whether he plays and how he is used. Canales said Tommy Tremble had his best game and credited growth in his relationship with Bryce Young, and he said Derrick Brown's reduced snap share is by design. He also said Jaelan Phillips is being evaluated for a hamstring and calf issue, with a full report due Wednesday. The coach expects Baker Mayfield to play for Tampa Bay if healthy but is preparing for Jalen Tucker-style alternatives, and he described the short turnaround for the Thursday game in Green Bay.

title: Zac Taylor: "Our Guys Get Really Fired Up For This Game" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Colbie Young looks close to full health and is set to re-enter the rotation, while Bryan Cook is nearing full strength; Kyle Dugger's status remains uncertain before the Baltimore game.
summary: Taylor said Kyle Dugger is progressing but his availability is still undetermined. He confirmed a player was sick but did not give details. During the bye, the staff self-scouted and began preparing for Baltimore, focusing on turnovers as the key AFC North stat because they drive field position. He called the divisional rivalry a fun, familiar matchup with both teams having new schemes but similar core ideas. He said the offense has a sense of identity centered on scoring on every drive, while the full three-phase complete game is still coming together. On the receiving corps, he said the coaches would combine the tight end and receiver rooms and distribute roles week to week, with the whole room in play as healthy players return. Colbie Young looked as good as he has in a long time, ran well in practice, and is nearing full health. Bryan Cook is moving much better and is closer to full strength, which helps against Baltimore's physical backs and mobile quarterback. Taylor also said that Tanner Hudson's absence leaves a gap that Young's return partly fills, since their roles overlap in some situations.

title: HC Sean Payton ahead of Week 7: ‘We’ve got a chance to play better this upcoming weekend’
headline: Payton stands by Bo Nix, says no QB change is being considered, and ties the offense's vertical struggles to the coaching staff and the offensive line's play, so Nix's fantasy outlook depends on a run-game and line rebound.
summary: Payton said the team knew Week 6 would bring challenging looks against a two-deep, two-high shell, and he took responsibility for not creating enough chunk plays downfield. He said the offense will get the ball downfield, and that the staff must give the passing game chances when they appear. Asked about changing quarterbacks, he said no, and that Bo Nix's play will improve as a byproduct of better offensive line play and a more efficient running game. He acknowledged the frustration and body language around the offense, especially when the team is not getting first downs, and said attention to detail has to improve. On the training room, he credited the staff's science and said mental toughness is part of the process, pointing to Nix's ability to climb through adversity as a reason the team drafted him. When asked about the national criticism of Nix, Payton said he is focused on preparing for Arizona. The team is 4-2 and expects to play better in Week 7.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'He balled out'
headline: Josh Jacobs' return timeline is still undecided and will hinge on the rest of the week, while Jordan Love gets strong praise after the Dallas win.
summary: LaFleur praised Jordan Love's performance in the 23-13 win over Dallas, saying he 'balled out' while taking hits and stood in the pocket despite earlier abuse. He said the offensive line improved but still busted some protections, and that drops remain a recurring problem. On the roughing-the-passer debate, LaFleur said the team reviews calls to educate players, and he defended Love's hits as legal while acknowledging a Karl Brooks hit that looked like body weight. Josh Jacobs was on the commissioner's exempt list and will sit out Wednesday's practice before getting a full week of practice, with his game readiness and any snap limits to be determined. LaFleur called Jacobs an elite back who can provide a spark. Kevin Zeitler is improving and getting more comfortable with the scheme, but his status is day to day. LaFleur praised Evan Williams' interception and Coleman Owen's punt return work, while criticizing Matthew Golden's option-route read and a missed tackle-down opportunity on a play where the whistle never blew. The run game remains a work in progress, and LaFleur said the team has ideas to fix it but is keeping them internal.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Tank Dell’s Return, C.J. Stroud & Giants Week
headline: Tank Dell is set to return Sunday vs. the Giants after two-plus years out, and Ryans says he's been impressive in practice; Reed Blankenship is in concussion protocol.
summary: Ryans credited C.J. Stroud for the offense's strong play, citing his progressions, ball security, and distribution to many receivers. He said the receivers' versatility and the offensive line's improved pass protection and run blocking, which produced over 100 rushing yards in London, have been key to the unit's success. He called the offensive line better each week and said Stroud's trust in them is clear in the pocket. On defense, Ryans said tackling is 'not good enough' and must improve quickly, especially against the Giants' physical backs, and he said the slick Wembley surface and Jacksonville's game plan contributed to the struggles. Tremon Smith earned player-of-the-game honors for stepping into the nickel and outside corner and making two critical stops. Ryans confirmed Tank Dell will play Sunday against the Giants after two strong weeks of practice, and said he expects Dell to stress defenders with his speed. Reed Blankenship is in concussion protocol, while Azeez Al-Shaair finished the game and is fine. Foster Moreau's two touchdowns were praised as a product of his energy and practice habits.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 6 recap, Colts vs. Titans
headline: Daniel Jones remains the starter vs. Minnesota, but Sauce Gardner (calf, week to week) and Alec Pierce (won't practice this week) are injury concerns.
summary: Steichen opened by praising GM Chris Ballard, whose firing he called the hard part of the business, and said the decision falls on the whole football operation, not Ballard alone. He said owner Carly Irsay told him of the decision and that he remains focused on the Vikings, though he gave no detail on his own job security beyond gratitude for being in the building. He told the team the Colts are 2-4, that they dug the hole together and must dig out together, and he compared it to his first year when a 3-5 start ended one play short of the division. Asked about roster or lineup changes, he said the team evaluates everything but the immediate focus is Week 7. Steichen confirmed Daniel Jones will start Sunday and that the defensive play-calling will continue under the current arrangement. On injuries, he said Sauce Gardner (calf) will be week to week after meeting with trainers, and Alec Pierce, still eligible to come off IR, is still in rehab and will not practice this week. He said the team has Tuesday off and returns Wednesday, and that players will need to block out outside noise. On Jones, he said the quarterback knows he must produce, with turnovers and red-zone decision-making the main issues.

title: Liam Coen Speaks Monday after Loss to Texans | Press Conference
headline: Coen praised rookie Nate Boerkircher's expanding role and Trevor Lawrence's play, while Josh Cameron is seeing heavy usage after the 34-31 loss to Houston.
summary: Coen used the bye-week media session to review the team after the 34-31 loss to the Texans. He said rookie Nate Boerkircher made a red-zone play and has been getting more playing time, and he hopes to keep building on that. He said Josh Cameron is playing a lot of football for the team, and he wants to keep getting Brian Thomas Jr. more reps as he contributes on special teams. He also praised Emmanuel Pregnon's inside play and said the defensive linemen from practice did strong work in preparing for the London game. On offense, Coen said the team was more efficient, ran the ball effectively, and protected well, but wants more explosive plays on the ground. He said he is very pleased with Trevor Lawrence. On defense, the Texans' jumbo personnel and run game gave the unit trouble, and Coen said the team gave up more runs than its standard, which he called humbling. He cited Kaevon Merriweather as someone who has not played much and said the coaches need to help settle the pass rush and simplify calls.

title: Sean McVay, Tyler Higbee & Quentin Lake discuss injury updates after Week 6, taking accountability, positive takeaways from Sunday & more
headline: Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks with a torn semitendinosus, and Poona Ford (season-ending) and Kobie Turner (a handful of weeks) are also out; Trent McDuffie is questionable and gets re-evaluated later this week.

A third key player also tore his ACL and is done for the season, though the transcript does not clearly name him. McVay said the locker room is disappointed but resilient, noting the team has lost three straight one-score games and must play more consistent, higher-quality football. He acknowledged the self-inflicted penalties, including offsides on a fourth-and-3 and at the start of Arizona's two-minute drive, and took responsibility for them. On defense he praised the red zone stand (opponents 0-for-5) and holding Arizona to six field goals. He said the staff is working on receiver options and expects a decision within a day or two, and that the offense may need week-to-week adjustments without Adams. On Trent McDuffie, he said he is progressing and feeling much better, with his status to be determined at the end of the week. Terrance Ferguson has no imminent return, but he is rehabbing and attending meetings.

summary: Kubiak said the Raiders' third-quarter scoring problems and red zone inefficiency were unacceptable, and the staff is reviewing halftime preparation and what it asks players to do coming out of the break. He called the offense's failures in the red zone a mix of penalties, a dropped ball, a missed fourth-and-one, and poor execution, with the run game the biggest need. He said Mike Washington had a strong game and that the backs as a group ran hard and broke tackles, and he expects continued improvement. He said Tre Tucker is showing he can stretch the defense and agreed that pushing the ball downfield opens things up. He praised Tyler Linderbaum as a leader and a major bright spot, and called Michael Mayer a productive, accountable leader who does dirty work. Kubiak said Caleb Rogers was prepared but still has good and bad moments as a young player, and that Spencer Burford has been a great addition who keeps improving. He said Darien Porter has thick skin after being benched and returning, and that he likes him. He described the team as 3-3 and said everything is still in front of them heading into a home game this week.

title: WATCH: The Mike McCarthy Press Conference Show presented by PNC (Week 7)
headline: McCarthy says Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren will keep sharing the field, and he is hopeful DeShon Elliott plays Sunday against New Orleans.
summary: McCarthy praised Jalen Ramsey's versatility and football intelligence, noting he can play across the back seven and made a key sack at the end of the game. He said the team is in regular contact with the league about the Paris trip, that a Zoom call with the league office was held with the whole team, and that he is confident in the security plan. The team will travel Thursday, and McCarthy said they chose that schedule after weighing both options. He called rookie Germie Bernard's game-winning day "outstanding" and said the young players will likely play bigger roles as the season goes on. On the injured DeShon Elliott, McCarthy said he hopes Elliott can return this week after a strong week of practice. He said he likes both Dowdle and Warren and wants both to touch the ball, which is why they were on the field together. McCarthy also said he trusts the depth receivers and the two Brandons, but he did not name a specific replacement plan for the injured receivers. He framed the Tampa win as a valuable road result that came through adversity, and said the team needs to clean up third-down conversions.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I’m Excited About Where We Can Go"
headline: Anthony Bradford could return to a significant role at right guard this week, Zach Charbonnet has a full week of reps and may play Sunday, and Elijah Arroyo is expected to be out a long time.
summary: Mike Macdonald said Monday's first day back from the break went well and that the team is more aligned after several days of honest conversations with Sam Darnold, Jake Peetz, Brian Fleury and Cooper Kupp. He framed the frustration after the loss as coming from a lost sense of Seahawks identity and said the team's problems are symptoms of fundamentals within their control, using tackling as the example. On scheme, he said the plays themselves are fine and the issues are in how they choose, get to and execute them. He said the team can do better at not falling into deep second-half holes and at knowing when to play faster versus stay in normal operation. Anthony Bradford is close to returning, and Macdonald said a good week would mean a large snap share at right guard. Zach Charbonnet will get a full week of practice reps and could play Sunday in some capacity. Elijah Arroyo will be out a significant time, with options being finalized and a decision, possibly IR, expected Wednesday. Macdonald also praised Darnold's consistency and leadership and gave Velus Jones Jr. positive but limited praise.

title: Todd Bowles on Baker Mayfield’s Timeline to Return | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield's Week 7 status is unresolved: he practices Wednesday, and Tampa Bay is preparing both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels. David Walker's role is expected to keep growing.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs have played well defensively but must finish games, and the offense has to catch up, especially in the fourth quarter. He defended the choice to kick in overtime and said the defense needed to close out the game rather than get extra rest. He pointed to missed assignments and two tackling breakdowns as the reasons the offense moved the ball better late. On A'Shawn Robinson lining up like an edge rusher, he tied it to the four-three front and using a bigger player on the edge to help against the run. Baker Mayfield is scheduled to practice Wednesday, and Bowles will evaluate him through the week before deciding on Sunday. Both quarterbacks are in the meetings while the staff waits to see how the week goes. David Walker's usage has increased every week, and Bowles said the staff intends to give him more reps, though game plans and personnel can limit that. He said Walker was third in the pass-rush rotation in that package. Bowles was critical of punter Riley Dixon's hang time and distance and said yesterday's performance did not reflect what he can do. The next game is a critical division matchup against Carolina, and Bowles stressed that winning is necessary to get back into the race.
